stem: Which pair has the same relationship as ABUNDANT : PLENTIFUL?
hints: ABUNDANT means there is a lot of something. How is it related to PLENTIFUL?
Make a bridge sentence: "Abundant means the same as plentiful."
Test each pair in the bridge "___ means the same as ___." Cross out opposites, and pairs where one word only describes the other.

solution.methodName: Make a bridge sentence, then test each choice

steps.action: Make a bridge sentence: "Abundant means the same as plentiful."
steps.why: Both words mean "more than enough". For example, rice is abundant after a good harvest. They are synonyms.

steps.action: Test ancient : modern. Ancient means very old and modern means new. They are opposites, so the bridge fails.
Test fragile : glass. Fragile means easily broken. It describes glass, but it does not mean the same as glass.
Test eager : unwilling. Eager means wanting very much to do something. Unwilling is nearly the opposite, so the bridge fails.
Test vacant : empty. "Vacant means the same as empty" is true.
steps.why: A vacant seat or a vacant post has no one in it. It is empty.

trapNotes.ancient : modern: These words are opposites. The stem words mean the same thing, so an opposite pair does not match.
trapNotes.fragile : glass: Fragile describes glass, because glass breaks easily. But a word and the thing it describes are not synonyms.
trapNotes.eager : unwilling: Eager means keen to do something, and unwilling means not wanting to. They are nearly opposite, not the same.
